c.tagline: Where the Silk Road meets snow-capped Tian Shan peaks.

taxi.fareNote: Most rides are booked via Yandex Go or inDrive with fixed upfront pricing; hailed street taxis should have a fare agreed before departure.

emergency.note: Fire is 101; the unified emergency number 112 also connects to all services.

hood_landmark.Kok-Tobe / Bostandyk: Kok-Tobe Cable Car Lower Station, Almaty

avoid.reason: Watch for pickpockets around the Green Bazaar and on crowded buses, and skip unofficial street taxis late at night.

hood_desc: The historic heart of Almaty around Panfilov Park and Zenkov Cathedral, packed with museums, cafes and Soviet-era architecture; ideal for first-time visitors who want to walk everywhere.
The bustling commercial core near Republic Square and the Zhibek Zholy pedestrian street, with department stores, restaurants and nightlife; suits travelers who want energy and easy transit access.
A leafy, embassy-lined avenue of upscale malls, cafes and business hotels; good for business travelers and those wanting a quieter, polished base close to shopping.
Almaty's glossy modern financial district around Esentai Mall and Almaty Tower, with fine dining and designer boutiques; suits luxury travelers and business visitors.
A green, hillside area near the Kok-Tobe cable car and Central Stadium with mountain views; good for families and travelers who prefer a quieter, local vibe.
lodging: Best Western Plus Atakent Park Hotel

water.note: Treated but quality is inconsistent; bottled, boiled, or filtered water is recommended for visitors.

transit.pay: Fares on the metro, buses and BRT are paid with the contactless Onai smart card (tap to reload and ride) or by tapping a bank card/phone directly at the turnstile or validator; single-use paper tokens are also sold at metro stations. Cash is generally not accepted on board buses.
transit.hours: Metro runs about 6:20am-midnight daily; most city buses operate roughly 6am-11pm with a few late-night routes; taxis and ride-hailing apps run 24/7.
transit.note: The single metro line covers only part of the city, so buses and ride-hailing apps are essential for getting around.

airport.name: Almaty International Airport (ALA)
airport.drive: 20-30 min to city center in light traffic; up to 45-60 min during rush hour

tip.r: Not traditionally required, but rounding up or leaving 5-10% at restaurants is increasingly common and appreciated where no service charge is included.
